parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. RESEARCH SUMMARY: In 5 sentences, summarize what you have found in your research. Use synthesis language (according to multiple sources, however, in conclusion, etc.).
2. VOCABULARY SPIRAL (W99-W105): Review quiz — Define 5 words: [synthesize / paraphrase / citation / reliable / bibliography]. Give one example sentence for each.
3. MATH SPIRAL: Review your data from research. Find 3 statistics (numbers, percentages) from your research notes. Write them as: 'X% of ___ + source'. Are these statistics from reliable sources?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Peer review is when you ask a classmate to read your work and give feedback. It is one of the most powerful learning tools because your peer can catch mistakes that you might miss, and offer a fresh perspective.
content: 📖 Peer review is when you ask a classmate to read your work and give feedback. It is one of the most powerful learning tools because your peer can catch mistakes that you might miss, and offer a fresh perspective.

Good feedback is SPECIFIC. Instead of 'This is good,' say 'The way you used evidence in paragraph 2 is very clear.' Instead of 'This is bad,' say 'I think paragraph 3 needs more evidence — could you add another source?'
Good feedback is KIND. Even when you disagree with someone's work, always find something positive to say first, then suggest improvements politely.
Good feedback is USEFUL. Focus on the most important issues, not every small mistake. Ask questions: 'What do you mean by...?' 'Could you explain...?'
After receiving feedback, you do not have to accept ALL suggestions. Decide which feedback will truly improve your work and explain why.
(↑ Re-read the story above to answer:)
